chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Al-Wassafi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
It was among what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, whispered to Musa (peace be upon him): He said, 'O Musa! Honour the beggar with a small gift or with a beautiful reply.'

Because there will come to you one who is neither human nor Jinn, an Angel from the Angels of the Beneficent, who will test you regarding what I have bestowed upon you and ask you about what I have given you.
So see how you are dealing, O son of Imran.
ai.seo_question: Why should one honour a beggar even with a small gift or kind words?
ai.summary: In this *munajat* (divine whisper) recorded in *Al-Kafi*, Allah instructs Prophet Musa (AS) to honor the beggar with either a modest gift or a gracious reply, emphasizing that the quality of one's response is as meritorious as the material act itself. The narration highlights a unique eschatological or worldly test where an Angel of the Beneficent, distinct from humans and Jinn, observes these interactions to evaluate how Musa manages the blessings (*nu'um*) Allah has granted him. This underscores the Shia scholarly view that charity is not merely transactional but a spiritual trial of gratitude and humility before the Divine.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, from Al Wassafy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘It was among what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Whispered with to Musa<sup>as</sup>, He<sup>azwj</sup> Said: “O Musa<sup>as</sup>! Honour the beggar with a little grace or with a beautiful return,

because there would be coming to you one who is neither a human being nor a Jinn, an Angel from the Angels of the Beneficent to Test you<sup>as</sup> regarding what I<sup>azwj</sup> have Bestowed on you<sup>as</sup> and he would be asking you<sup>as</sup> about what We<sup>azwj</sup> have Given you<sup>as</sup>.
Therefore consider how you<sup>as</sup> are dealing, O son<sup>as</sup> of Imran<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from al-Wassafiy from abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who has said the following:

“Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, spoke to Moses about certain matters. Of such matters, one was this: ‘O Musa (Moses), treat one asking for help graciously, with a little charity or send him away with kind words;

one who is not of man or Jinn may come to you who, in fact, is an angel of the angels of the Beneficent. He may come to examine and test you about the favors that I have granted you. They ask you of the favors I have granted to you.
Consider, O son of ’Imran, how you behave.’”
